title: audit_iss103_test.zig TC-ISS-103-INT-02/03/04 fail because the harness's GBL-081 compatibility shim disables ALL triggers on audit-covered tables, so no audit_entries rows are ever created
summary: Discovered incidentally while verifying the ISS-0091 (GitHub #343) migration-tracker-unification fix via zig build test-integration-iss103. Independent of ISS-0091 and not caused by it: tests/integration/helpers.zig::applyCompatibilityShims() (see helpers.zig ~lines 209-231) runs ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER ALL against tenant_default.process_definitions, instance_projections, tasks, dead_letter_items, webhook_subscriptions, and webhook_deliveries -- with a comment explaining this works around a GBL-081 type mismatch (audit_entries.resource_id changed from uuid to text, but the audit trigger function bpm_audit_compute_chain_hash still expects uuid for that parameter). Because DISABLE TRIGGER ALL disables every trigger on those tables including the audit-chain trigger, no audit_entries rows are ever inserted for any test that goes through TestHarness.init() -- so tests/integration/audit_iss103_test.zig's TC-ISS-103-INT-02 (idx_audit_resource index enables efficient point lookups), TC-ISS-103-INT-03 (mixed resource types are all queryable by TEXT resource_id), and TC-ISS-103-INT-04 (audit entries clean up without leftover data) all fail their `count/before_cleanup >= 1` assertions, because the very audit_entries rows they expect the system to have created were never created due to the trigger being disabled. Confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to ISS-0091: reproduces identically on baseline main (pre-ISS-0091-fix) and on the ISS-0091 fix branch (tests/integration/helpers.zig's migration-related functions were changed by ISS-0091, but applyCompatibilityShims() was not touched).

root_cause.details: GBL-081 (audit_entries.resource_id uuid->text) left bpm_audit_compute_chain_hash()/bpm_audit_chain_canonical_payload() with stale uuid-typed parameters, causing type-mismatch errors on INSERT into any table with the audit trigger attached. migrations/GBL-082_fix_audit_chain_resource_id_text.sql already corrects both function signatures to TEXT (confirmed by inspection: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION bpm_audit_chain_canonical_payload(..., p_resource_id TEXT, ...) and comment '1. Update bpm_audit_chain_canonical_payload to accept TEXT resource_id'). However, tests/integration/helpers.zig::applyCompatibilityShims() still unconditionally runs ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER ALL against tenant_default.process_definitions, instance_projections, tasks, dead_letter_items, webhook_subscriptions, and webhook_deliveries on every TestHarness.init() call, with a comment describing the now-already-fixed GBL-081 type mismatch as the reason. This shim was never removed after GBL-082 landed, so it continues to defeat audit-chain trigger behavior for every integration test, including the audit_iss103_test.zig suite that specifically exists to verify that behavior.

files_to_change: tests/integration/helpers.zig -- remove (or narrow to only the tables that still need it, if any) the ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER ALL shims in applyCompatibilityShims(), since GBL-082 already fixed the underlying type mismatch that motivated them

tests/integration/audit_iss103_test.zig -- re-verify TC-ISS-103-INT-02/03/04 pass once triggers are re-enabled; if any other currently-passing test relied on triggers being disabled (e.g. to avoid unrelated trigger side effects), that dependency must be identified and handled explicitly rather than via a blanket disable

occurrences.context: Found while running zig build test-integration-iss103 to verify the ISS-0091 migration-tracker-unification fix did not regress other direct-migration-caller test files. Confirmed identical failure on baseline main -- unrelated to and not caused by the ISS-0091 change. Confirmed by reading migrations/GBL-082_fix_audit_chain_resource_id_text.sql that the underlying type mismatch was already corrected; the compatibility shim in helpers.zig::applyCompatibilityShims() was simply never removed afterward.

Re-verified the full diagnosis against current main/feature branch state before handing off to CODE-DESIGNER. (1) tests/integration/helpers.zig::applyCompatibilityShims() (lines 208-230) still runs 'ALTER TABLE IF EXISTS tenant_default.<table> DISABLE TRIGGER ALL' unconditionally for process_definitions, instance_projections, tasks, dead_letter_items, webhook_subscriptions, and webhook_deliveries, and is called unconditionally from TestHarness.init() (line 481) before every test's transaction begins. (2) migrations/GBL-082_fix_audit_chain_resource_id_text.sql confirmed to redeclare both bpm_audit_chain_canonical_payload(...) and bpm_audit_compute_chain_hash(...) with p_resource_id TEXT (was UUID pre-fix). (3) tests/integration/audit_iss103_test.zig confirmed: TC-ISS-103-INT-02 (line 230), TC-ISS-103-INT-03 (line 307), TC-ISS-103-INT-04 (line 430) all assert audit_entries row counts (count/typed_count/count1/count2 >= 1, and after_cleanup == 0) that require the bpm_audit_on_mutation() trigger to have fired on process_definitions INSERT. (4) Traced the full causal chain via migrations/020_obs03_audit_entries.sql (CREATE TRIGGER ... EXECUTE FUNCTION bpm_audit_on_mutation() on process_definitions/instance_projections/tasks/dead_letter_items/webhook_subscriptions/webhook_deliveries) and migrations/035_adp09_tamper_evident_audit_chain.sql (trg_bpm_audit_apply_chain_hash on audit_entries itself, calling bpm_audit_compute_chain_hash). The shim's DISABLE TRIGGER ALL on the six business tables prevents bpm_audit_on_mutation() from ever firing, so audit_entries never receives rows in tests -- independent of whether the downstream chain-hash function's parameter type is now correct. (5) Checked every migration after GBL-082 (GBL-083 through GBL-101, plus 081-094 numeric series) for any reintroduced uuid/text mismatch or any other legitimate reason to keep triggers disabled on these six tables: none found. GBL-084_rls_removal.sql touches audit_entries/audit_log and process_definitions/instance_projections/webhook_subscriptions/webhook_deliveries/dead_letter_items only for RLS policy removal and tenant_id column drop in the public schema -- it does not touch trigger attachment and does not affect tenant_default. No migration after GBL-082 references bpm_audit_compute_chain_hash or bpm_audit_chain_canonical_payload again. (6) Searched docs/issues/*.json and issue_index.json for other local registrations mentioning 'compatibility shim', 'GBL-081', 'GBL-082', or trigger-disable patterns: only ISS-0093 itself and a forward cross-reference from ISS-0091's resolution text (which explicitly names ISS-0093/GitHub #346 as filed separately) were found; no conflicting or duplicate registration exists. Diagnosis confirmed accurate as originally written, with no corrections needed to files_to_change.

resolution: Removed the stale GBL-081 'ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER ALL' compatibility shim from tests/integration/helpers.zig::applyCompatibilityShims() (the type mismatch it worked around was already corrected by migrations/GBL-082_fix_audit_chain_resource_id_text.sql). Fixed audit_iss103_test.zig's own cleanup helper to disable/enable USER triggers only (not ALL triggers) around its DELETE, matching the audit-log-immutability-respecting pattern already used in xc02_audit_immutability_test.zig. TC-ISS-103-INT-01..04 moved from 0/4 to 4/4 passing, confirmed in isolation and inside the full aggregate zig build test-integration suite. RELEASE-VALIDATOR independently verified zero of the 134 aggregate-suite failures are attributable to this change (all trace to two pre-existing, separately-filed defects -- ISS-0094/#348, ISS-0095/#349 -- or the known ISS-0090 aggregate-contention pattern). GitHub issue #346 closed via squash-merge of feature/WF03-iss0093-20260731.
prevention: When a compatibility shim is added to work around a bug (here: disabling triggers to avoid a type-mismatch error), track the shim itself as a follow-up issue at the time it is added, and re-verify the corresponding test suite specifically (not just 'tests pass overall') once the real fix believed to obsolete the shim has landed -- a shim that outlives its corrective migration silently defeats the very tests meant to verify that migration's effect.

This resolution itself produced two more follow-up issues (ISS-0094, ISS-0095) discovered only once the shim's masking effect was removed -- confirming the pattern: a shim doesn't just hide its own bug, it can hide other, unrelated bugs underneath it too. Removing a long-lived shim should always be followed by a broader-than-minimal verification pass (full aggregate suite, not just the originally-targeted tests), which is what surfaced both follow-ups here.
